subject: Post-demo follow-up: incident response comparison & hands-on failover tests

Subject: Post-demo recap + ops/escalation playbook (next steps)

Hi Alice / Mark —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum while your team evaluates incident response and escalation behavior across providers.

Use case summary (from our call)
- Low-latency inference for customer-facing personalization (P99 target ~120ms)
- Strong requirement for predictable failover across regions and clear RCA timelines for audits
- Data residency + KMS-managed keys for key customer subsets

What Cloudoria asked us to compare
- Support hours & on-call routing vs hyperscalers (Vertex/Bedrock)
- SLA credit model and how SLOs map to mitigation actions
- Typical forensic / RCA timelines and redaction/anonymization for sharing examples

Proposed immediate deliverables from Redwood
1) Ops & escalation playbook (attached): high-level runbook, on-call escalation ladder, sample alerting thresholds. See attachment: redwood-ops-playbook-v1.pdf
2) Redacted RCA example for a prior P99 incident (attached) — Sergio will redact and share a template we can use for your audit team
3) Hands-on failover test: we propose a controlled failover on Dec 18 or 21 (you pick one) to run circuit-breaker + region-routing behavior and capture traces
4) Comparison one-pager that contrasts our incident response cadence and SLAs with the major hyperscalers (we’ll highlight differences in RCA cadence and ownership)

Ask for you: please confirm who on your side should be invited to the failover test (ops, infra, security) and which of the two dates works. Also confirm whether you prefer the RCA example in PDF or a short redacted playbook.

Next internal steps (for transparency)
- Sergio: Prepare redacted RCA and technical notes
- Marissa: Draft the 1-page incident response comparison vs hyperscalers
- Jordan: Schedule the failover test in our test environment and send runbook

Looking forward — we’ll be ready to run the test and capture the artifacts your auditors requested.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Hi Alice — thanks for the specific questions. Quick answers and what we can provide ahead of the failover test: 

1) 24/7 on-call 
- Enterprise customers can opt into 24/7 paging; this is part of our Premium Support add-on (usually included in Dedicated / Private plans at the SLA tier).

2) SLA credit model
- Credits are applied as a percentage of monthly invoice for sustained violations of P99 latency or availability SLOs. We calculate credits based on incident duration and severity tiers; I’ll include the exact formula in the one-pager.

3) RCA cadence
- Initial findings (triage summary): typically within 48-72 hours for incidents with clear telemetry.
- Full RCA (including timeline, root cause, mitigation, and follow-up actions): target within 7-10 business days for complex infra incidents. We can accommodate accelerated timelines for audit windows on a case-by-case basis.

4) Forensics & redaction
- We can produce a redacted RCA (remove customer-specific data, IPs, request traces) and provide a sanitized timeline. Attached is a redacted example from a prior customer (sample-redwood-rca-redacted.pdf).

5) Failover runbook and measurable success criteria
- Jordan will run a controlled region failover in our staging environment. Success criteria we propose: 95%+ service continuity within 30s for new connections, KV cache warmup within two minutes, and no data plane errors for pinned customer sessions. Capture distributed traces and KV cache hit rates.

If Cloudoria wants, we can also include a short appendix that highlights where hyperscalers differ operationally (e.g., longer managed-incident handoff windows, fewer guarantees around redaction timelines because of cross-tenant log retention policies). We’ll make that a short, neutral comparison.

Let me know if you want the initial redacted RCA sent over now or after we finalize the one-pager.

--
Sergio Alvarez
